title: HighDimensionalBlockHeterogeneousNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a differentiable function on Euclidean space. The two-sided quadratic Taylor remainder bound permits negative curvature. The objective has a global lower bound ℓ satisfying f(x₀) − ℓ ≤ Δ.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: One call at an adaptively chosen x returns the full vector g(x, ξ), including every block, with E[g(x, ξ)] = ∇f(x). Each call uses a fresh i.i.d. real seed. Blocks within a reply may be dependent. All parameters d, B, blk, L, σ, Δ, ε and x₀ are public. The objective, oracle map and seed law are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalBlockHeterogeneousNonconvex.lean, Params, toGeneral and spec.publicInput. LongTails/Setups/BlockHeterogeneousNonconvex.lean, spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x and block j, E‖Pⱼ(g(x, ξ) − ∇f(x))‖₂² ≤ σⱼ², where Pⱼ is the orthogonal projection onto the coordinates assigned to j. Each σⱼ is nonnegative and may vanish.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is ℝᵈ with B > 0 coordinate blocks. Writing S = Σᵢ Lᵢ and H = Σᵢ(Lᵢσᵢ²)^(1/3), every individual block must contain at least 2⁴⁰(1 + BSΔ/ε² + H³Δ/ε⁴)⁴ coordinates.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The block smoothness constants control simultaneous displacements. For every x and h, |f(x+h) − f(x) − ⟨∇f(x),h⟩| ≤ ½ Σⱼ Lⱼ‖Pⱼh‖₂². Every Lⱼ is positive, ε > 0, and 2⁵⁷ε² ≤ LⱼΔ for every block.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: At the algorithm’s output X, the stationarity measure is Σⱼ‖Pⱼ∇f(X)‖₂, the sum of unsquared Euclidean block norms. X may be any output point in ℝᵈ.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: X must be measurable, the stationarity measure must be integrable, and E[Σⱼ‖Pⱼ∇f(X)‖₂] ≤ ε under the joint law of algorithm and oracle randomness.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup pairs a separate curvature and noise bound for each public block with a sum-of-block-norms stationarity criterion. It also imposes a parameter-dependent minimum dimension on every block.

descriptionHtml:
High-Dimensional Blockwise Stochastic Stationarity

We seek a stationary point of a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R in dimension d. Its linearization error admits a quadratic bound with a separate coefficient for each coordinate block, and its value at a given starting point lies within a prescribed gap of a global lower bound. Each block has a prescribed minimum dimension. At any query point, the oracle returns an unbiased gradient estimate from a fresh independent real sample, with bounded mean squared error in each block. For tolerance ε>0, the goal is a measurable output whose sum of Euclidean block-gradient norms has expectation at most ε over algorithm and oracle randomness.

The underlying optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x). A map b:{1,…,d}→{1,…,B} assigns each coordinate to a block. Write Ij={i:b(i)=j} and let Πj be the orthogonal projection onto the coordinates in Ij. The algorithm receives the integers d,B≥1, the map b, the block parameters Lj>0 and σj≥0 for 1≤j≤B, the gap bound Δ>0, the tolerance ε, and the starting point x0∈Rd.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Scale and block dimensions). Write S=∑i=1BLi and T=∑i=1B(Liσi2)1/3. Every block j satisfies LjΔ≥257ε2,|Ij|≥240(1+BSΔε2+T3Δε4)4.

Assumption 2 (Blockwise quadratic bound and initial gap). The function f is differentiable throughout Rd. For all x,h∈Rd, |f(x+h)−f(x)−⟨∇f(x),h⟩|≤12∑j=1BLj∥Πjh∥22. There exists ℓ∈R such that f(x)≥ℓ for every x∈Rd and f(x0)−ℓ≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic gradient oracle). At each query x∈Rd, the oracle returns g(x,ξk), where k indexes the call and g:Rd×R→Rd is jointly Borel measurable. The real random variables (ξk)k≥1 are independent with common law ν, and the sequence is independent of the algorithm’s randomness. For ξ∼ν, write e(x,ξ)=g(x,ξ)−∇f(x). At every x, the vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable, each ∥Πje(x,ξ)∥22 is integrable, and Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[∥Πje(x,ξ)∥22]≤σj2,1≤j≤B.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯∈Rd must be measurable under the joint law P of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle samples. The stationarity measure ∑j=1B∥Πj∇f(x¯)∥2 must be integrable under P and satisfy EP[∑j=1B∥Πj∇f(x¯)∥2]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
On Rd with B≥1 coordinate blocks, f(x0)−inff≤Δ and |f(x+h)−f(x)−⟨∇f(x),h⟩|≤12∑jLj∥Pjh∥22 for all x,h. Each call returns a jointly measurable, unbiased gradient estimate g(x,ξ) using a fresh i.i.d. real sample, with E∥Pj(g(x,ξ)−∇f(x))∥22≤σj2. The target is E∑j∥Pj∇f(x^)∥2≤ε. For (1), each block satisfies 257ε2≤LjΔ and dj≥240(1+BD+V)4, with ε,Lj>0 and σj≥0.

High-dimensional block-heterogeneous nonconvex optimization: lower bounds on necessary gradient calls.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations

(2) (Arjevani et al. 2022), Thm. 3 and Sec. 1.3 Ω(maxjLjΔε2(1+σj2ε2)). Derived bound, one active high-dimensional block. (1): Equal Lj,σj amplify the deterministic term by B and the noise term by B3 over (2). Same order when one block dominates the sums. (1) needs the accuracy and dimension conditions in every block. (2) needs sufficient dimension and ε≲LjΔ only in the active block.
(3) (Jiang et al. 2025), Thm. 5 Ω(∥L∥1Δ/ε2). Deterministic algorithms, exact gradients, scalar blocks. (1) retains the noiseless order for every randomized algorithm on high-dimensional blocks. With noise, its additional term dominates when S3>ε2∥L∥1. (1) requires large blocks and small ε in every block. Its noiseless prefactor is 2−57, versus 1 in (3) for the strict target ∥∇f∥1<ε.
(4) AdaGrad (Jiang et al. 2025), Thm. 4 Ω((D+V)log⁡(1+D+V)) as ε↓0 at fixed problem parameters. Scalar blocks, δ=0, best queried iterate. (1) establishes the same polynomial dependence for arbitrary randomized algorithms and outputs on high-dimensional blocks, matching the block-SGD upper bound there up to constants. (1) excludes scalar blocks. The AdaGrad-specific lower bound in (4) has an additional logarithmic factor.

import LongTails.Setups.BlockHeterogeneousNonconvex
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.Basic

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalBlockHeterogeneousNonconvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  B : ℕ
  blk : Fin d → Fin B
  L : Fin B → ℝ
  σ : Fin B → ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

noncomputable def toGeneral (q : Params) : LongTails.Setups.BlockHeterogeneousNonconvex.Params where
  d := q.d
  B := q.B
  blk := q.blk
  Ω := ℝ
  L := q.L
  σ := q.σ
  Δ := q.Δ
  ε := q.ε
  x0 := q.x0

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) → ℝ
  Query q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Reply q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Output q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.B ∧ (∀ j, 0 < q.L j) ∧ (∀ j, 0 ≤ q.σ j) ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧
    (∀ j, 2 ^ 57 * q.ε ^ 2 ≤ q.L j * q.Δ) ∧
    ∀ j, 2 ^ 40 * (1 + q.B * (∑ i, q.L i) * q.Δ / q.ε ^ 2 +
      (∑ i, (q.L i * q.σ i ^ 2) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)) ^ 3 * q.Δ / q.ε ^ 4) ^ 4 ≤
        (Fintype.card {i // q.blk i = j} : ℝ)
  admissible q f O :=
    LongTails.Setups.BlockHeterogeneousNonconvex.spec.admissible (toGeneral q) f O
  successful q f output P :=
    LongTails.Setups.BlockHeterogeneousNonconvex.spec.successful (toGeneral q) f output P

end LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalBlockHeterogeneousNonconvex
